segments.source: This shortlist solves a physical fit problem: fitting an electric espresso-capable grinder beside a machine and still reaching its controls, beans and cleaning parts. We included only exact reviewed models with current manufacturer width, depth and height data, a US configuration, and enough independent use evidence to discuss a limitation. We excluded grinders with missing comparable dimensions or a larger body that did not improve this particular decision. The dimensions are manufacturer body specifications, not measurements taken by Coffeedant.

segments.source: Measure the countertop from backsplash to usable front edge, then the gap from counter to cabinet underside. Reserve room around the grinder for a cup or portafilter, a hand on the adjustment, its power cord, and safe access to remove beans and clean the burr chamber. A body that fits exactly on paper can be awkward under a low cupboard. None of the three published dimensions proves that the top-opening or bellows can operate within the same height. Make a cardboard rectangle for the footprint before ordering.

segments.source: The three bodies are all narrow, at 130–133 mm wide, but their proportions differ. The Encore ESP Pro is the shallowest on the stated dimensions at 150 mm deep; it is 340 mm tall and its hopper or single-dose lid and adjustment collar are above the body. Opus 2 is 267 mm tall, yet 206 mm deep. The Zero 65 All Purpose is 357 mm tall and 215 mm deep, before any practical clearance for its bellows. Those figures are useful for screening a shelf, not a complete installed-space drawing.

segments.source: Counter placement also determines which control feels convenient. Opus 2 uses a side adjustment dial; check which side remains reachable next to your espresso machine. The Baratza changes grind at the upper collar and presents a front display. Eureka has a large marked dial and a dosing fork, but the bellows needs space above. A tight counter can make the theoretically smaller grinder harder to use if the accessible side faces a wall.

segments.source: Opus 2 is the most natural fit for someone who weighs a fresh dose for every espresso and sometimes grinds filter coffee. Fellow supplies two magnetic catch cups and describes the espresso cup as compatible with 54 mm and 58 mm portafilters. That is a cup-transfer statement, not universal portafilter fit: different baskets, handles and funnels still matter. Its one stepless dial removes the older Opus inner-ring routine. The Coffee Chronicler liked its speed and low mess on a particular sample, but found its plastic grind chamber and filter cup less convincing.
segments.context: Opus 2 is the most natural fit for someone who weighs a fresh dose for every espresso and sometimes grinds filter coffee. Fellow supplies two magnetic catch cups and describes the espresso cup as compatible with 54 mm and 58 mm portafilters. That is a cup-transfer statement, not universal portafilter fit: different baskets, handles and funnels still matter. Its one stepless dial removes the older Opus inner-ring routine. The Coffee Chronicler liked its speed and low mess on a particular sample, but found its plastic grind chamber and filter cup less convincing. [1] [4]

segments.source: The Encore ESP Pro can keep beans in a hopper for timed doses or run a single-dose mode. That flexibility matters in a cramped shared kitchen where weighing every serving may be impractical. The independent Expert Reviews sample worked across espresso and filter, but its empty-hopper stop sometimes required a manual stop, and initial disassembly was awkward. Do not infer a failure frequency for every unit from one reviewer. Check that the collar can be reached and the hopper removed in your actual cabinet gap.

segments.source: The Eureka Zero 65 All Purpose is the specialist choice for a narrow station where careful espresso adjustment and occasional brewing changes justify a bellows routine. Its 65 mm flat burrs, stepless micrometric setting and revolution counter are exact-model features. The bellows can help clear loose grounds, yet independent Kaffeemacher measurements show that “Zero” is not literal empty retention. The substantial 5.6 kg body also makes frequent lifting to clear a cabinet less attractive.

segments.source: All three need access for periodic cleaning. A grinder pushed hard against a backsplash or trapped under a fixed shelf invites skipped maintenance, especially when the hopper or burr assembly must come off. Follow the exact manual, unplug first, and keep water away from electrical and burr components unless that manual explicitly permits it. A brush, bellows or anti-static feature reduces a particular mess; none replaces scheduled cleaning.

A brush, bellows or anti-static feature reduces a particular mess; none replaces scheduled cleaning. [7] [8] [9]

segments.source: The Encore ESP Pro’s independent disassembly difficulty deserves weight if hand strength or access is limited. Fellow describes tool-free burr access, which is convenient on paper, while its plastic chamber is a material tradeoff. Eureka’s bellows and cup add steps to the morning routine. Plan space for the accessories as well as the body; a compact machine surrounded by loose cups and funnels is not a compact station.

segments.source: A shallow grinder may let you retain a usable prep zone, while a shorter body may fit a cabinet. Either saving is valuable only if the grind quality and daily routine meet your espresso needs. Keep room in the setup budget for a scale, a compatible cup or funnel, and a sensible cleaning kit. Avoid buying a larger hopper or dosing accessory until the body has been placed and used. For a travel kit or a counter with no safe electrical space, the separate reviewed K-Ultra hand grinder may be a better category entirely, with hand effort as its explicit cost.

segments.source: Yes, their makers specify espresso-capable adjustment. Actual basket, beans and recipe determine the setting; the guide does not claim a side-by-side taste result.
segments.context: text

segments.source: Does the Eureka bellows leave zero coffee inside?
segments.context: name

segments.source: No. The independent sample study found nonzero retained coffee under its protocol. A bellows helps a workflow but does not prove a completely empty path.
segments.context: text

segments.source: Can I keep the Baratza hopper under a low cabinet?
segments.context: name

segments.source: Only if there is room to load beans, turn the collar and remove parts for cleaning. Measure the clearance in your kitchen beyond the published 340 mm body height.
segments.context: text

segments.source: Are these current US price rankings?
segments.context: name

segments.source: No. This guide uses no unverified numeric price or discount. Confirm the exact finish, voltage, availability and delivered total in the live US cart.
segments.context: text
